item.title: Riviera Travel Opens 2028 Worldwide Collection with New Long-Haul Destinations
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Riviera Travel has released its 2028 Worldwide Collection earlier than ever, anchored by three brand-new, expert-guided itineraries: a 16-day deep dive into Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego, a 15-day island-hopping journey through Indonesia’s temples and volcanic landscapes, and a comprehensive tour of French Canada paired with Niagara Falls. The early launch directly addresses growing market research showing that while modern travelers increasingly crave deep, authentic cultural immersion, they strongly prefer having structured local guidance to navigate unfamiliar customs and complex logistics. Beyond the three headline additions, the operator has also expanded its dedicated solo travel portfolio with specialized versions of its popular China, Silk Road, and Southern Africa itineraries.

The Curated Take

Releasing a 2028 long-haul program years in advance reflects a growing industry trend: experienced travelers are securing complex, bucket-list itineraries earlier than ever. By pairing remote expedition destinations like Patagonia and Komodo National Park with the safety net of an escorted tour and built-in cultural guidance, Riviera Travel addresses a key market sweet spot—delivering deep, immersive cultural exploration without the logistical friction of traveling entirely on your own.

item.title: Sweden is Building a Floating Soundwave to House Its First National Music Museum
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Sweden is finally giving its staggering global music legacy a dedicated national home, with the Swedish National Music Museum set to open in the coastal town of Västervik in July 2027. Despite consistently ranking among the world’s top three exporters of music, the country has never had a single national hub to chronicle its journey from local community arts programs to global chart domination. Designed by architecture firm OKIDOKI, the two-story, 8,600-square-foot floating structure will anchor in the Baltic Sea next to the historic Stegeholm castle ruins. Its exterior is designed to look like a “frozen soundwave” made of pulsating timber panels that mirror audio rhythms.

Choosing Västervik over Stockholm brings the museum directly to the roots of the “Swedish Music Miracle.” Spearheaded in part by ABBA legend and Västervik native Björn Ulvaeus—who owns the neighboring sustainable Slottsholmen resort—the museum lands right in the heart of Sweden’s historic folk music capital. Located about 174 miles south of Stockholm, the floating museum will break down how a small nation produced global hits from ABBA to Max Martin, alongside tech titans like Spotify. Visitors can immerse themselves in interactive exhibits before stepping outside to explore the surrounding 5,000-island Tjust Archipelago.

The Curated Take

For decades, Sweden has quietly written the soundtrack to American pop radio, yet its music history has remained scattered across individual band museums and local legends. By building a dedicated national monument over the Baltic Sea, Sweden is framing its music culture not as a series of lucky pop hits, but as a deliberate, national art form. The fact that you can tour state-of-the-art interactive exhibits on a floating architectural soundwave, step out onto the deck, and hop a ferry straight into a 5,000-island archipelago turns a simple museum visit into one of the most compelling cultural road trips in Europe.

item.title: Sundance Mountain Resort Expands Terrain with New High-Speed Quad and Ridgeline Run for 2026/2027 Season
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Sundance Mountain Resort is expanding its winter footprint with the addition of over 100 acres of new terrain, marked by a high-speed quad lift named Electric Horseman and a signature 1.7-mile groomed ridge run named Storyteller. This milestone marks the completion of the resort’s first phase of back mountain expansion, bringing its total skiable area to 605 acres while setting the stage for future expert terrain growth. Servicing over 1,850 vertical feet in just six minutes, Electric Horseman significantly boosts uphill capacity and provides direct access across the back mountain.

Carved out of the former Far East Ridgeline, the new Storyteller run delivers an upper-intermediate grooming experience complete with mountain vistas, while also providing advanced skiers access to three new tree-lined gladed chutes. The expansion honors the creative heritage and vision of founder Robert Redford, building upon a series of recent multi-year capital improvements—including the Outlaw Express Lift, expanded snowmaking systems, and the new Mountain Camp Day Lodge.

The Curated Take

Sundance has long been cherished for its intimate, art-infused sanctuary feel, but limited terrain and older lift infrastructure sometimes meant sacrificing lap counts for ambiance. This major back-mountain expansion strikes a ideal balance: by adding a high-speed quad that slashes transit times to six minutes and opening up 100+ acres of ridgeline and tree runs, the resort elevates its technical ski offering without losing the boutique, soul-driven identity that sets it apart from Utah’s mega-resorts.

item.title: Nuju Uluwatu Opens in Bali, Joining Preferred Hotels & Resorts’ Exclusive L.V.X. Collection
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
A new sanctuary has arrived on Bali’s southern peninsula with the official opening of Nuju Uluwatu, an adults-only resort now inducted into Preferred Hotels & Resorts’ prestigious L.V.X. Collection. Derived from the Indonesian word meaning “towards,” Nuju celebrates the vast architectural and artistic diversity of the entire Indonesian archipelago rather than limiting itself to traditional Balinese aesthetics. Designed around traditional home forms with layered rooflines and tropical gardens, the property’s accommodations range from One-Bedroom Pool Suites paying homage to Western Indonesia with rich green tones and handcrafted batik, to Cabanas and Signature Residences reflecting Eastern Indonesia through blue hues and hand-woven Flores textiles.

The wellness-focused resort weaves traditional culture into every facet of the guest experience, offering immersive batik painting workshops, classical storytelling, and regional dance alongside a full spa, sauna, cold plunge pools, and modern fitness spaces. At the center of the resort sits Sana, an open-concept venue serving Modern Australian cuisine inflected with bold Asian flavors, spanning an indoor dining room, lounge, and poolside garden.

The Curated Take

Uluwatu’s clifftop hotel scene can often skew toward slick, generic modernism, but Nuju stands out by grounding its design in authentic Indonesian heritage. By drawing architectural elements, textile traditions, and artistic craftsmanship from islands across the entire archipelago—and reserving the sanctuary strictly for adults—the resort delivers a deeply serene, culturally rich escape that feels far more soulful than typical luxury openings.

item.title: Atlanta Beltline Reaches Historic 17-Mile Milestone Ahead of 2026 World Cup
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Beltline celebrated a landmark 20th-anniversary milestone with the official opening of Southside Trail Segments 2 + 3, creating an uninterrupted 16.7-mile continuous loop known as “The U.” The newly opened 1.9-mile stretch links Pittsburgh Yards to Boulevard, bridging the Eastside and Westside trails and reconnecting 36 historic Atlanta neighborhoods across the Northwest, Westside, Southside, Eastside, and Northeast sectors. Backed by over $31 million in federal and regional funding, the accelerated project delivers crucial transit infrastructure just in time for the city to host eight FIFA World Cup 2026™ matches.

First envisioned in 1999 as a 22-mile urban loop along historic freight rail lines, the Beltline has grown into one of the country’s most ambitious redevelopment initiatives. The project functions as the world’s longest linear arboretum in partnership with Trees Atlanta, serves as the city’s largest outdoor arts destination, and has spurred over $14 billion in private investment. With 16.7 miles of mainline trail and 10.3 miles of connector paths now open, the project remains on track to complete the final 4.7 miles of the full 22-mile loop by 2030.

The Curated Take

The completion of “The U” transforms what was once a series of disconnected neighborhood path segments into a truly unified urban transport artery. By linking historic Southside neighborhoods to existing Eastside and Westside hubs ahead of the global spotlight of the 2026 World Cup, Atlanta demonstrates how infrastructure-led multi-use paths can redefine urban mobility, drive equitable economic development, and establish a new benchmark for linear green spaces worldwide.

Photo Credit Atlanta Beltline, Inc. Photo by Erin Sintos

item.title: Four Seasons Hotel Singapore Reimagines Communal Dining Across Its Iconic Venues
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Four Seasons Hotel Singapore has launched a new lineup of communal dining experiences designed to elevate the art of gathering. Across its flagship restaurants, the property is focusing on shared spreads, interactive live stations, and bespoke group menus. At Nobu Singapore, the weekend offerings expand with the Sunday Sushi Social—featuring hand-pressed nigiri and signatures like Black Cod Miso—alongside the lavish Taste of Nobu Saturday Brunch, complete with an F1 Japanese Beef live station and an optional 90-minute After Brunch cocktail extension at Nobu Bar.

Guests seeking refined Chinese and Italian flavors have equally compelling options for shared dining. Michelin-selected Jiang-Nan Chun introduces “Taste of Hong Kong,” a communal concept by Executive Chinese Chef Alan Chan featuring handcrafted dim sum, comforting noodles, and regional delicacies like Steamed Pork Dumplings in Laksa Sauce. Meanwhile, One-Ninety Restaurant introduces two distinct concepts: an intimate Chef’s Table experience for groups up to 14 featuring a customized six-course Italian tasting menu, and the Convivio Weekend Brunch, a generous semi-buffet loaded with fresh seafood, artisanal cold cuts, tableside-served secondi, and elaborate dessert displays.

The Curated Take

Modern luxury dining is undergoing a clear shift away from rigid, overly formal individual plating in favor of lively, shared culinary experiences. Four Seasons Hotel Singapore captures this momentum brilliantly by turning high-end gastronomy into an interactive social centerpiece. Whether you are gathering a group for a front-row seat at One-Ninety’s Italian Chef’s Table or settling into a multi-hour Japanese-Peruvian brunch spread at Nobu, these new offerings prove that high-end hospitality hits highest when it centers on abundance, connection, and the simple joy of breaking bread together.

item.title: Taste the Ocean and Dine in a 19th-Century Church in West Sweden
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
West Sweden is rolling out two brand-new experiences that combine world-class gastronomy with unmatched local heritage. Seafood lovers can now head to the seaside town of Grebbestad—Sweden’s undisputed “Oyster Capital”—for a guided culinary walking tour hosted by Skärgårdsidyllen. Taking place during the prime chilly water months between September and April, the two-to-three-hour stroll takes foodies through six distinct tasting stops. Participants get to sample iconic local delicacies, from fresh-shucked wild oysters and sweet crayfish to pickled herring, seaweed, local brews, and a traditional Swedish fika.

Further inland, culture hounds can pull up a seat inside a repurposed 1875 church situated on the slopes of the Kinnekulle plateau, about 93 miles northeast of Gothenburg. Now known as Österplana Agriturismo, the deconsecrated house of worship has been meticulously transformed into a farm-to-table restaurant and venue. Diners feast beneath soaring vaulted ceilings on tables built out of original church pews, enjoying hyper-seasonal menus crafted from the surrounding countryside and nearby Lake Vänern.

The Curated Take

Travelers are increasingly burning out on generic dining rooms and canned city tours, craving immersive culinary stories with a sense of place instead. West Sweden is tapping directly into that desire by turning both nature and history into interactive dining tables. Whether you’re slurping world-class shellfish straight from cold ocean waters or sipping wine beneath historic stained-glass architecture, these new offerings showcase how thoughtful, localized tourism can transform a standard getaway into a unforgettable cultural experience.

Photo Credit Kristina Gillerstedt / westsweden.com

item.title: Plan Ahead: La Résidence Phou Vao Unveils Exclusive Advance Booking for Luang Prabang Sanctuary
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
High atop a serene hill overlooking the UNESCO World Heritage town of Luang Prabang, La Résidence Phou Vao, a Luxury Collection Resort & Spa, is celebrating its newest chapter with an exclusive incentive for forward-thinking travelers. Known for its French colonial architecture, lush tropical gardens, and an award-winning infinity pool framed by views of Mount Phousi and the Mekong River valley, the resort has launched “The Advance Reservation.” Available to book through September 30, 2026, for stays throughout 2026, this early-booking offer rewards guests with a suite of curated perks designed for effortless exploration and relaxation.

Guests booking under the special rate enjoy daily breakfast at La Brasserie de la Résidence, complimentary non-alcoholic minibars, dedicated guest experience planning, and seamless round-trip airport or railway transfers. Stays between October and March unlock extra high-value perks, including a $50 resort credit, daily sunset apéritifs with French canapés, complimentary daily laundry service, and a three-course dinner for stays of three nights or more. Paired with convenient daily shuttles into town, the resort provides an ideal launchpad for taking in Luang Prabang’s gilded temples, night markets, and traditional Lao spa treatments at the open-air Mekong Spa.

The Curated Take

Luang Prabang has long been a crown jewel for slow, intentional travel, but finding a sanctuary that balances high-end luxury with authentic cultural immersion can be a delicate task. La Résidence Phou Vao nails this balance by pairing colonial elegance with one of the most iconic infinity pool views in Southeast Asia. By packaging thoughtful, high-friction logistics—like transfers, laundry, and daily town transport—into an early booking incentive, the resort makes planning a seamless, bucket-list Asian getaway remarkably straightforward for luxury travelers.

Photo Credit La Résidence Phou Vao, A Luxury Collection Resort & Spa

item.title: Kansas City, Kansas Celebrates the First Anniversary of Its Famous Barbecue Trail
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Barbecue lovers have a delicious reason to hit the road as the KCK BBQ Trail marks its official one-year anniversary. Launched by Visit Kansas City Kansas on September 19, 2025, the mobile-exclusive passport has drawn massive engagement, generating over 1,700 pass downloads and 850 check-ins across Wyandotte County. Featuring 12 primary stops and two bonus locations, the self-guided trail celebrates everything from iconic heavyweights like Joe’s Kansas City and Slap’s to beloved neighborhood joints like Quentin’s BBQ & Sides, Roscoe’s, and Woodyard.

To celebrate the milestone, organizers are upping the stakes for hungry travelers. Any participant who checks in at five or more stops by September 1 earns an exclusive invite to the trail’s official birthday party on September 17. Plus, completing five stops enters trail-goers into a grand prize drawing valued at over $1,000, which includes a Napoleon Freestyle 3-burner propane gas grill paired with a deluxe at-home barbecue kit. The free mobile pass allows visitors to explore Wyandotte County’s distinct culinary neighborhoods while tracking down burnt ends, slow-smoked brisket, and legendary ribs.

The Curated Take

Food trails can sometimes feel like gimmicky marketing stunts, but the KCK BBQ Trail hits the mark by honoring the hyper-local roots of Midwestern pitmaster culture. Rather than funneling tourists into a single crowded dining district, this passport encourages travelers to explore the true culinary footprint of Wyandotte County—from long-standing family joints to neighborhood spots serving up incredible burnt ends. Gamifying the experience with solid prizes and a low barrier to entry turns a simple lunch stop into an engaging, multi-neighborhood road trip centered on legendary smoked meats.

Photo Credit Visit Kansas City Kansas

item.title: Frontiers North Adventures Unveils Fully Renovated Tundra Inn in Churchill, Manitoba
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Frontiers North Adventures has officially revealed an extensive renovation and expansion of the historic Tundra Inn, a cornerstone of subarctic hospitality in Churchill, Manitoba. The refreshed property nearly doubles its capacity, growing to 44 total guest rooms (including 21 newly constructed accommodations). Designed with modern travelers in mind, the upgrades feature refined room configurations with king and loft layouts, a fully accessible main-floor room, keyless entry, smart TVs, and bedside charging stations. Guests returning from polar bear, beluga whale, or northern lights excursions can unwind in a welcoming new lobby or dine just steps away at the Ptarmigan restaurant, which serves modern subarctic cuisine.

The opening marks a major reinvestment in Canada’s “Polar Bear Capital of the World,” providing contemporary comfort while maintaining the cozy charm and local hospitality for which the property is known. Owned and operated by sustainable tourism leader Frontiers North Adventures, the Tundra Inn is fully open and welcoming guests for the autumn polar bear viewing season and year-round subarctic adventures.

The Curated Take

Remote, bucket-list travel to extreme climates like Churchill often forces travelers to choose between authentic subarctic access and high-end lodging comfort. Frontiers North Adventures bridges that gap masterfully with the Tundra Inn’s transformation. By pairing essential modern amenities—like keyless entry, loft configurations, and accessible design—with regional culinary experiences and local hospitality, the property elevates the entire destination. It provides wild-frontier explorers with a refined, comfortable sanctuary to return to after a day out on the tundra.

Photo Credit Frontiers North Adventures / Tundra Inn
